# Retire the never-read grid token --grid-container-header-cell-border-bottom

## Context

Found while reviewing #20638. Its example stylesheet sets `--grid-container-header-cell-border-bottom`, following the Workstation palette bridge, and the line has no effect.

## The Problem

Every grid theme defines `--grid-container-header-cell-border-bottom`, and an app stylesheet sets it, but no stylesheet ever reads it. `git log -S` over the whole history finds no `var(--grid-container-header-cell-border-bottom` and no SCSS `v(grid-container-header-cell-border-bottom`. The token has had no consumer since #3412 introduced it on 2022-08-30.

What draws the header's bottom border today is `resources/scss/src/grid/header/Toolbar.scss:2`, using `--grid-container-border-color`. So an app that sets this token to restyle that border sees nothing change. The Workstation palette spec asserts the token's inherited value, which passes whether or not anything renders it.

## The Architectural Reality

Every site on `dev`:
- definitions: `resources/scss/theme-{neo-light,neo-dark,light,dark,cyberpunk}/grid/Container.scss:10`;
- setter: `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss:53` (#17987's bridge);
- assertion: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL.spec.mjs:53`;
- if #20638 merges first: `resources/scss/src/examples/grid/headerGroups/MainContainer.scss:11`.

## The Fix

Delete the token at every site above, including its row in the Workstation palette spec. Nothing reads it, so nothing renders differently.

Wiring it up as the header's bottom border instead would change the header in every theme (`theme-dark` declares `2px`) and would need a design read. That is not this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git grep -- --grid-container-header-cell-border-bottom` returns nothing.
- [ ] `WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL.spec.mjs` passes without the row, and no visual golden changes.

## Out of Scope

Any change to the header's bottom border. An audit of other theme tokens that nothing reads.

## Related

#20638 (where it was found) · #3412 (introduced) · #17987 (the Workstation bridge that sets it)
